messages.content: What are the different properties of Hydrogen?

message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average; varies by isotope) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | | **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV | | **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (121.5 K) at 1 atm | | **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.0 K) at 1 atm | | **Density** | 0.08988 g/L at 25 °C, 1 atm | | **Molar volume** | 22.414 L/mol (ideal gas at STP) | | **State at room temperature** | Gas | | **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (4–75 % H₂ in air) | | **Solubility in water** | ~1.6 g/L at 25 °C (low) | | **Isotopes** | • **Protium** (^1H): most common, no neutrons.
• **Deuterium** (^2H or D): one neutron, ~0.015% natural abundance.
• **Tritium** (^3H or T): two neutrons, radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 y). | | **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic molecules (H₂) are the most stable form under normal conditions. | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; reacts with oxygen to form water (exothermic). Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). | | **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). | | **Applications** | • Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells).
• Industrial processes (ammonia synthesis, petroleum refining).
• Scientific research (spectroscopy, plasma physics).
• Space propulsion (liquid hydrogen rockets). | **Additional Notes** - **Physical State:** Hydrogen exists as a diatomic molecule (H₂) under standard conditions. It is the lightest element and has the lowest boiling and melting points among all elements. - **Chemical Behavior:** As a nonmetal, hydrogen typically forms +1 oxidation state compounds (e.g., H₂O, CH₄). In metal hydrides, it often exhibits a -1 oxidation state. - **Isotope Effects:** Deuterium and tritium exhibit slightly different physical properties due to their higher masses, affecting reaction rates and spectroscopic transitions (isotope shift). - **Safety:** Hydrogen is colorless, odorless, and highly flammable. Proper ventilation and handling protocols are essential when working with it, especially in high concentrations or pressurized containers. These properties make hydrogen unique among elements and central to many scientific, industrial, and energy-related applications.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What are the different properties of Hydrogen?" They want properties of hydrogen. We can provide general chemical and physical properties. But we also have a tool to look up major contributions of a particular scientist. That doesn't apply here. So we just answer with properties. Provide a list: atomic number, mass, electronegativity, ionization energy, electron affinity, boiling point, melting point, density, etc. Also mention isotopes: H-1, H-2 (deuterium), H-3 (tritium). Also mention its behavior as a gas, flammability, etc. Provide a concise but thorough answer.

We should not call the tool. Just answer.
